transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Dir Eng - Mercury), Priya Rao (SRE Lead - Mercury), Luca Romano (CTO - Mercury)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Mercury Finance is evaluating Redwood for a mix of Hosted and Dedicated, with eye towards Private for regulated European flows. Key focus on reliability, multi-region failover, and incident tolerance.
- Primary concerns: automated failover timing, SLA credits, routing policies, and data residency/KMS when using Private.
- Next steps: whitepaper, pricing, demo with failover, sample traffic/benchmarks.

Topics: reliability, multi-region routing, fallbacks, SLAs, Private deployment, KMS/encryption, benchmarking

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone — thanks for carving out time. quick intro, i'm jordan from Redwood, AE. with me is sofia, our solutions engineer. how are you all?
00:07 Alex: pretty good, thanks. alex here. we wanted to focus the call on reliability, how you do failover, and what our options are between hosted/dedicated/private.
00:14 Priya: yeah, our SRE team has some questions around routing policies and how automatic the fallbacks are.
00:20 Jordan: perfect. that's exactly what we wanted to cover. so, very high level first — can you share current setup and what your availability targets are?
00:30 Alex: sure — we run a mix of managed endpoints for inference today, some internal k8s-ish clusters, traffic is north america heavy, but about 20% europe. p95 latency target for UX is 300ms, p99 is 800ms. 99.95% uptime expected from any vendor ideally.
00:46 Luca: and we have regulatory constraints for EU traffic, so we may need data residency for that subset. also keys have to be customer-managed for production.
00:56 Sofia: got it. so there's three knobs that matter: routing (region to region), model fallbacks (e.g., fallback to smaller quantized model if top-tier is unavailable), and deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private). we can do combinations.
01:14 Priya: can you walk through a typical incident flow? like if us-east loses a gpu pool, what's the automatic behavior?
01:21 Sofia: yeah. in hosted, our control plane monitors cluster health and we have routing policies. by default requests route to nearest healthy region, and we have automatic fallback rules. if a primary model becomes unavailable we can route to a compatible variant (same architecture, possibly quantized) and we automatically fall back to a different region after connection errors or elevated latency thresholds. there are configurable thresholds — e.g., after 5 consecutive 5xx or 3 consecutive p95 breaches we consider it degraded and route.
01:50 Alex: are those thresholds configurable per-customer? we'd want a faster failover for checkout flows.
01:55 Jordan: yes, we expose per-route policies in the console and via API, so you can tune sensitivity. templates for low-latency paths recommended for checkout.
02:04 Priya: what's the typical failover latency? like how long between detection and successful routing to another region?
02:10 Sofia: it depends on what you tune, but operationally we've seen automated DNS-ish routing within a few hundred milliseconds to a few seconds for in-cluster rerouting; cross-region might add 50 to 200ms additional RTT. realistic end-to-end failover times customers observe are often 2–5s for a clean switchover in hosted. for Dedicated you can get faster tail behavior because you're on reserved capacity and we can keep warm standby replicas.
02:36 Luca: that 2–5s is probably okay for async features, but for checkout we need sub-second. any options?
02:42 Sofia: for sub-second we recommend either Dedicated with regional standby or Private with colocated replicas in both regions and local health checks, plus a global LB in front that does active-active routing. we can also implement client-side retries to immediate local fallback to reduce perceived latency.
03:00 Alex: what about model-variant fallbacks — do outputs degrade a lot when you fall back to smaller models?
03:07 Sofia: depends on the model & quantization. we maintain variant performance profiles; often the fallback is a same-arch quantized model with slightly higher error rates but similar semantics. we also provide quality monitoring and alerting so you can detect regression in production. many customers prefer a graceful degrade (slightly lower accuracy) over total outage.
03:28 Priya: are these fallbacks automatic or do you require us to opt-in?
03:32 Jordan: both. there are safe defaults we enable for platform resilience, but you can opt-in to aggressive fallbacks or lock them down to require manual approval — it depends on how conservative you want to be.
03:41 Alex: on SLAs — you listed 99.95 in the doc; what does that buy us? credits? and does that apply across Hosted, Dedicated, Private?
03:50 Jordan: good question. hosted SLA is 99.95 with credits defined per downtime window; Dedicated can be higher depending on contract (99.97+ with reserved capacity), and Private is contractually defined because it's customer-managed infra though we do provide support SLAs for our control plane. SLA credits are standard — percentage of monthly invoice prorated. we'll share the exact SLO/SLA doc.
04:10 Luca: and if an incident is due to cloud provider network, how does Redwood's fallback handle provider-wide outages?
04:17 Sofia: we do multi-cloud and multi-region routing; for provider-wide events we can route to a different cloud region or provider if you have capacity there — that's more common with Dedicated or Private when you provision across clouds. Hosted supports cross-region within the provider and fallbacks to our replicated regions. worst-case there's manual escalation and cross-region failover.
04:39 Priya: security: can we bring our KMS for Private? we need HSM-backed keys.
04:44 Jordan: yes — for Private we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and we can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping depending on plan. we'll include the KMS integration doc.
04:58 Alex: on logging and audits, do you provide per-request audit logs? our compliance folks need traceability.
05:04 Sofia: yes — we capture request metadata, model version, latencies, and error codes. logs can be shipped to your SIEM or stored in the Redwood console with configurable retention. for Private we can forward to your internal logging.
05:17 Alex: great. any certifications? SOC 2? ISO?
05:21 Jordan: we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO 27001 in process; we'll send the compliance packet.
05:27 Priya: another question — how do you handle burst capacity? sometimes we have sudden spikes — do you autoscale across regions?
05:33 Sofia: yes, autoscaling works per-region with burst capacity options. Dedicated includes burst pools you can configure for peak windows. we also do request prioritization so critical routes can preempt lower-priority workloads during congestion.
05:48 Alex: curious about observability — can we see token-level latency and cost per route?
05:52 Sofia: yes, Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. we can instrument span ids so your traces link to Redwood requests.
06:02 Luca: about testing failover — can we run a staged failover test without impacting production?
06:07 Jordan: absolutely. we support canary rollouts and manual failover drills. Sofia: we can orchestrate a simulated region outage in our staging environment and run your traffic profile against it.
06:18 Alex: that would help. please include a test plan in the materials.
06:21 Sofia: will do.
06:24 Priya: do you do health checks on the model itself or only infra-level? e.g., model drift or performance regressions?
06:30 Sofia: both. infra healthchecks detect node and service failures. model quality monitoring can be set up by feeding evaluation prompts and running quality regressions; Redwood Optimize can alert on regressions tied to prompt sets and will auto-trigger rollbacks if configured.
06:47 Alex: any limits on model variants — say we want two versions per route for quick fallbacks?
06:52 Jordan: you can register multiple model variants per route; routing policies let you prefer version A and fallback to B, or traffic split for canary.
06:59 Priya: network-wise, for Private we'd use VPC peering. do you require specific firewall rules or egress controls?
07:05 Sofia: yes we'll share a network configuration doc — typical requirements: outbound access to our control plane endpoints, specific ports for telemetry, and optional private link setup. exact rules depend on deployment.
07:18 Alex: pricing — can you ballpark cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our scale — roughly 200 qps peak, 2M tokens/day?
07:27 Jordan: rough rule: Hosted is usage-based and can be cheaper for variable workloads but less predictable. Dedicated has committed monthly and can reduce per-token cost by 25–50% depending on commit level. Private includes platform fee and infra. i'll put together a more precise estimate with your traffic numbers; send the sample profile and we'll model it.
07:44 Luca: what's required to pilot? timeline?
07:48 Jordan: we can do a 4–6 week POC: week 0 onboarding and access, week 1–2 integration and baseline benchmarks, week 3 failover/drill tests and performance tuning, week 4 review and decision. Dedicated pilot may require longer for capacity scheduling.
08:03 Priya: ok, one more — how do you handle caching of KV cache and prefix caching across regions? we want warm cache when failover happens.
08:11 Sofia: good point — our prefix and KV cache can be replicated asynchronously to standby regions; there's a tradeoff between consistency and latency. for very low-latency-critical routes we recommend active-active with lightweight state sync, or Dedicated with synchronous replication. we'll include our caching consistency options in the whitepaper.
08:31 Alex: thanks. anything else we should know about incident postmortems? do you own the RCA for hosted incidents?
08:37 Jordan: for hosted incidents we'll provide incident reports, timelines, and postmortems. for Dedicated we partner with your ops team. Private incidents are managed by customer but we assist with logs and diagnostics.
08:48 Priya: ok that clarifies.
08:50 Jordan: great. quick recap / next steps: sofia will share multi-region routing whitepaper and benchmark template; jordan will send pricing and SLA doc; mercury will send traffic profile and infra diagrams. we also scheduled a demo/failover drill for 2026-05-06 pending availability.
09:08 Alex: yes, that's accurate. thanks everyone.
09:11 Luca: thanks.
09:13 Priya: thanks, bye.
